note: Rewritten from the species description in Scheffrahn (2019), originally in English; the alate is recorded as unknown in the original; the measurement table was originally laid out in three columns 'maximum/minimum/mean' and is given here as an ascending range, with the values and means unchanged; figure numbers, type material, comparisons and the key are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier belongs to the long-mandibulate group (mandibles longer than the head capsule) and is closest to R. perarmatus but smaller: head length including nasus 1.73—2.20 mm, against 2.5—2.6 mm in R. perarmatus and 3.0—3.2 mm in its junior synonym R. major, i.e. 1.14—1.85 times larger; head capsule yellow rather than reddish brown; mandibles (including the marginal tooth) narrower and more slender; nasus more strongly curved, and segment 3 of the antenna relatively shorter. In the key the species is separated from R. perarmatus by 'head length including nasus ≤2.20 mm, head yellow' versus '≥2.5 mm, head reddish brown'. The worker is concolorous with the soldier, the frontal gland pore small and weak, less prominent than in R. perarmatus; the three enteric valve pads and the spines of the interpad regions are fewer, and the longitudinal folds and fringes anterior to the enteric valve of R. perarmatus are absent. Alates not seen.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Monotypic. Head capsule, nasus and mandibular bases straw yellow; apical and marginal teeth yellowish brown. Head capsule dome-shaped in profile. Nasus projecting distinctly beyond the mandibles, subcylindrical, tapering to a rather large rounded opening; hollow, with walls of uniform thickness. Head capsule pilosity limited to 2 weak setae near the level of the antennal sockets and 1—2 shorter, finer setae on the vertex; nasus bare, slightly curved downwards. Mandibles curved through about 150—180°, the strongest curvature behind the marginal tooth; tapering beyond the marginal tooth. Apical tooth very narrow and pointed; marginal tooth very thin, directed towards the labrum at about 60°. Antennae very long, about twice the length of the nasus; 14-segmented, 2<3>4=5. Pronotum slightly paler than the head; asymmetrically bilobed in dorsal view, the posterior lobe larger; in profile the edge of the anterior lobe continuous with the vertex and the posterior lobe humped. Fore coxa with a spine-like process, slightly curved downwards. Measurements (3 nests, 12 specimens, mm; range, mean): head length including nasus 1.73—2.20 (2.06), maximum head width 0.67—0.88 (0.81), pronotum width 0.37—0.56 (0.52), hind tibia length 1.19—1.54 (1.39), maximum left mandible length 0.61—1.05 (0.89), number of antennal segments 14.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Monotypic. Head capsule concolorous with the soldier. Head capsule with 8—10 long, evenly distributed setae; postclypeus strongly arched. In profile the posterior lobe of the pronotum much longer, forming an angle of about 130° with the plane of the posterior lobe. Antenna 14-segmented. Anterior margin of the fore coxa with a swelling. Enteric valve weakly spiny, consisting of 3 rectangular pads, each with 30—40 very small triangular spines; between the pads a broader cuticular lining scattered with still smaller spines. Measurements (3 nests, 12 specimens, mm; range, mean): head length to condyle 0.61—1.00 (0.79), head width 1.09—1.25 (1.17), pronotum width 0.58—0.70 (0.63), hind tibia length 1.16—1.37 (1.26), number of antennal segments 14.
